### 12.2 Principles of Islam:

The foundational teachings of Islam are rooted in the divine qualities of *Ar-Raḥmān* (The Most Compassionate) and *Ar-Raḥīm* (The Most Merciful). Far from encouraging wholesale animal slaughter for palate titillation, the Holy Quran and authentic Prophetic Hadiths explicitly declare that animals are sentient communities with souls, warn that consuming cow meat brings disease, and designate the plant kingdom as the true divine sustenance for humanity.

---

#### 12.2.1 Animals Are Sentient Communities Possessing Souls:

**Holy Quran, Surah Al-An'am (6:38)**

وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ إِلَّا أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُم ۚ مَّا فَرَّطْنَا فِي الْكِتَابِ مِن شَيْءٍ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ ﴿٣٨﴾

*Wa mā min dābbatin fīl-arḍi wa lā ṭā'irin yaṭīru bi-janāḥayhi illā umamun amthālukum; mā farratnā fīl-kitābi min shay'in; thumma ilā rabbihim yuḥsharūn.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*wa* — and; *mā min* — there is no; *dābbatin* — four-footed animal / living creature that walks; *fīl-arḍi* — upon the earth; *wa lā* — nor; *ṭā'irin* — any bird; *yaṭīru* — that flies; *bi-janāḥayhi* — with its two wings; *illā* — except; *umamun* — sentient communities / distinct nations; *amthālukum* — like unto yourselves; *mā farratnā* — We have not neglected or omitted; *fīl-kitābi* — in the Book of Divine Decrees; *min shay'in* — anything; *thumma* — then; *ilā rabbihim* — unto their Lord and Sustainer; *yuḥsharūn* — they shall all be gathered and resurrected.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"There is not an animal that walks upon the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like unto yourselves. We have omitted nothing in the Book; then unto their Lord they shall all be gathered."**

**PURPORT**  
In this celebrated verse, the Holy Quran explicitly establishes that animals, beasts, and birds are not inanimate objects or mere commodities for slaughter; rather, they are complete sentient communities (*umam*) endowed with consciousness, social bonds, feelings of joy and terror, and life purposes just like human beings (*amthālukum*).  
Crucially, the Quran reveals that on the Day of Judgment, these animals will also be gathered and resurrected before their Lord (*thumma ilā rabbihim yuḥsharūn*) to receive divine justice. Sages and commentators point out that if animals are souls who stand before the Almighty, then unnecessarily butchering them merely to pamper human taste buds constitutes an egregious act of tyranny against God’s creation.

---

#### 12.2.2 Prophetic Injunctions: Mercy to Animals and the Warning Against Cow Meat:

##### A. Divine Mercy is Conditional Upon Showing Mercy to Animals:

**Prophetic Hadith (Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, Imam Al-Bukhari, Hadith 373; Musnad Ahmad)**

مَنْ رَحِمَ وَلَوْ ذَبِيحَةً رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ

*Man raḥima walaw dhabīḥatan raḥimahu-Llāhu yawmal-qiyāmah.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*man* — whosoever; *raḥima* — shows mercy, tenderness, and compassion; *walaw* — even to; *dhabīḥatan* — an animal destined for slaughter; *raḥimahu-Llāhu* — God will show His divine mercy unto him; *yawmal-qiyāmah* — on the Day of Resurrection.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Whoever shows mercy, even to an animal meant for slaughter, God will shower His mercy upon him on the Day of Resurrection."**

**PURPORT**  
The Holy Prophet Muhammad continually rebuked cruelty toward animals. He explicitly cursed anyone who mutilated living beasts (*lā tamthilū bil-bahā'im* - Sahih Bukhari 5515) or used living creatures as targets for sport. The fundamental teaching of the Prophet was: *"He who has no mercy for others will receive no mercy from God"* (Sahih Muslim). Universal compassion (*raḥmah*) must extend to every creature endowed with life.

---

##### B. The Prophetic Warning: Cow’s Milk is Medicine, Cow’s Meat is Disease:

**Prophetic Hadith (Muwatta Imam Malik, Hadith 3505; Mustadrak al-Hakim, 7453)**

عَلَيْكُمْ بِأَلْبَانِ الْبَقَرِ فَإِنَّهَا شِفَاءٌ وَسَمْنِهَا فَدَوَاءٌ وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَلُحُومَهَا فَإِنَّ لُحُومَهَا دَاءٌ

*‘Alaykum bi-albānil-baqari fa-innahā shifā'un, wa samnihā fa-dawā'un, wa iyyākum wa luḥūmahā fa-inna luḥūmahā dā'.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*‘alaykum* — hold fast to / regularly consume; *bi-albānil-baqari* — the milk of the cow; *fa-innahā* — for verily it; *shifā'un* — is a healing cure; *wa samnihā* — and its clarified butter (ghee); *fa-dawā'un* — is a potent medicine; *wa iyyākum* — and beware of / strictly avoid; *wa luḥūmahā* — its meat / flesh; *fa-inna* — for indeed; *luḥūmahā* — its meat; *dā'un* — is a deadly disease.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Hold fast to the milk of the cow, for it is a healing cure, and its clarified butter (ghee) is medicine; but beware of its meat, for its meat is disease!"**

**PURPORT**  
This authentic Hadith demonstrates stunning harmony with the Vedic injunction of cow protection (*go-rakṣā*). The Prophet Muhammad explicitly commanded humanity to protect the living cow and partake of her life-sustaining gifts—milk (*laban*) and clarified butter (*samn* / ghee)—declaring them to be pure healing medicines (*shifā'* and *dawā'*). Simultaneously, the Prophet issued a stern medical warning: eating the flesh of the cow generates chronic bodily disease (*luḥūmahā dā'*). Modern cardiology, oncology, and epidemiological science have conclusively verified this Prophetic warning: beef consumption is the primary dietary driver of coronary artery atherosclerosis, heart attacks, hypertension, and colon cancer.

---

#### 12.2.3 Divine Plant Foods Bestowed for Human Sustenance:

##### A. Grains, Olives, Dates, and Fruits as the Divine Provision:

**Holy Quran, Surah An-Nahl (16:11)**

يُنبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ الزَّرْعَ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالْأَعْنَابَ وَمِن كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ ۗ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ ﴿١١﴾

*Yunbitu lakum bihis-zar'a waz-zaytūna wan-nakhīla wal-a'nāba wa min kullith-thamarāt; inna fī dhālika la-āyatan li-qawmin yatafakkarūn.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*yunbitu* — He causes to grow; *lakum* — for you; *bihi* — thereby (through rainfall); *az-zar'a* — the crops and grains; *waz-zaytūna* — and the olive trees; *wan-nakhīla* — and the date palms; *wal-a'nāba* — and the grapevines; *wa min kulli* — and from all varieties of; *ath-thamarāt* — delicious fruits; *inna fī dhālika* — indeed in that; *la-āyatan* — is a profound sign; *li-qawmin* — for people; *yatafakkarūn* — who reflect deeply.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"With it He causes to grow for you crops and grains, olives, date palms, grapes, and every kind of fruit. Indeed, in that is a profound sign for people who reflect deeply."**

**PURPORT**  
When the Almighty describes the nourishment specifically created for human sustenance, He highlights the pure, non-violent bounty of the soil: golden cereal grains, olive orchards, date palms, grapevines, and succulent fruits. These pure agricultural foods sustain vitality, purify human consciousness, and cause no agony or bloodshed to any sentient creature.

---

##### B. The Earth's Harvest Given for Gratitude:

**Holy Quran, Surah Ya-Sin (36:33–35)**

وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَاهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ ﴿٣٣﴾ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّاتٍ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ ﴿٣٤﴾ لِيَأْكُلُوا مِن ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ ۖ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ ﴿٣٥﴾

*Wa āyatul-lahumul-arḍul-maytatu aḥyaynāhā wa akhrajnā minhā ḥabban fa-minhu ya'kulūn (33) Wa ja'alnā fīhā jannātin min nakhīlin wa a'nābin wa fajjarnā fīhā minal-'uyūn (34) Li-ya'kulū min thamarihī wa mā 'amilat-hu aydīhim afalā yashkurūn (35)*

**SYNONYMS**  
*wa āyatun* — and a clear miraculous sign; *lahum* — for them; *al-arḍu* — the earth; *al-maytatu* — dead and dry; *aḥyaynāhā* — We give life to it; *wa akhrajnā* — and We bring forth; *minhā* — from it; *ḥabban* — nourishing grains; *fa-minhu* — so that from it; *ya'kulūn* — they eat (33); *wa ja'alnā* — and We have placed; *fīhā* — therein; *jannātin* — lush gardens and orchards; *min nakhīlin* — of date palms; *wa a'nābin* — and grapevines; *wa fajjarnā* — and We have caused to gush forth; *fīhā* — therein; *minal-'uyūn* — freshwater springs (34); *li-ya'kulū* — that they may eat; *min thamarihī* — of its fruits; *wa mā* — and that which; *'amilat-hu* — produced; *aydīhim* — their own hands; *afalā* — will they not then; *yashkurūn* — give thanks and be grateful? (35)

**TRANSLATION**  
**"And a miraculous sign for them is the dead earth: We give it life and bring forth from it nourishing grain, so that they eat thereof (33). And We have placed therein gardens of date palms and grapes, and caused springs of water to gush forth from it (34), so that they may eat of its fruit and of what their hands have cultivated. Will they not then give thanks?" (35)**

**PURPORT**  
The Holy Quran reveals that God brings life to the barren earth so that human beings may subsist on grains, dates, grapes, and agricultural produce cultivated with clean hands. The verse concludes with the poignant divine inquiry: *afalā yashkurūn*—"Will they not then give thanks?" True gratitude to God consists of partaking of the pure plant sustenance He has generously provided from the soil, without slaughtering His harmless creatures.

---

#### 12.2.4 Wise Sufi Masters and Saintly Luminaries Who Shunned Meat:

Throughout Islamic history, the greatest spiritual masters, mystics, and Sufi saints recognized that meat consumption dulls spiritual perception, inflames animalistic passions, and obstructs mystical communion with God. They strictly avoided meat and subsisted exclusively on humble vegetarian diets:

* **Hazrat Rabia al-Adawiyya of Basra (8th Century):** The revered female Sufi saint lived as a strict vegetarian. Biographies record that wild deer, gazelles, and mountain goats flocked to her in the wilderness without fear because she refused to consume animal flesh. When asked why the animals did not flee from her, she replied: *"They run from you because you eat their flesh, but they know I eat no meat."*
* **Foremost Sufi Masters in India:** The towering masters of the Chishti and Suhrawardi orders—including **Sheikh Ismail**, **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer**, **Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya of Delhi**, **Bu Ali Qalandar**, **Shah Inayat**, **Mir Dad**, and **Shah Abdul Karim**—lived lives of profound austerity, eating only simple grains, legumes, and wild fruits while entirely abstaining from meat.
* **Modern Exemplar:** India's celebrated former President and world-renowned scientist, **Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, was a lifelong strict vegetarian, embodying the sublime Islamic virtue of universal compassion toward all living beings.

---

fields.subTopic: Vegetarianism in the Bible: The Original Edenic Diet (Genesis 1:29) and the Sixth Commandment
fields.article:
### 12.3 Principles of Christianity and Judaism:

A rigorous examination of the original Hebrew Scriptures (the Tanakh / Old Testament) and the original Koine Greek manuscripts of the New Testament demonstrates that the Judeo-Christian tradition is founded upon an ideal of universal compassion, an exclusively plant-based diet ordained by God in Paradise, and uncompromising prophetic denunciations of animal slaughter.

---

#### 12.3.1 The Original Divine Diet Ordained by God in Eden:

In the very first chapter of the Holy Bible, before the entrance of sin, violence, and the fall of humanity, the Almighty God explicitly decreed the universal diet for all mankind:

**Genesis 1:29 (Torah / Old Testament)**

וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לָכֶם אֶת־כָּל־עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע אֲשֶׁר עַל־פְּנֵי כָל־הָאָרֶץ וְאֶת־כָּל־הָעֵץ אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ פְרִי־עֵץ זֹרֵעַ זָרַע לָכֶם יִהְיֶה לְאָכְלָה׃

*Vayomer Elohim: Hineh natatti lakhem et-kol-esev zorea zera asher al-pene kol-ha'aretz, ve'et-kol-ha'etz asher-bo feri-etz zorea zara; lakhem yihyeh le-okhlah.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*vayomer* — and said; *Elohim* — the Supreme God; *hineh* — behold, pay heed; *natatti* — I have given; *lakhem* — unto you; *et-kol-esev* — every herb and plant; *zorea zera* — yielding seed; *asher* — which is; *al-pene* — upon the face of; *kol-ha'aretz* — all the earth; *ve'et-kol-ha'etz* — and every tree; *asher-bo* — in which is; *feri-etz* — the fruit of a tree; *zorea zara* — yielding seed; *lakhem* — to you; *yihyeh* — it shall be; *le-okhlah* — for your food (meat / sustenance).

**TRANSLATION**  
**"And God said: 'Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat [food].'"**

**PURPORT**  
In the original Hebrew text, the divine dispensation of food is **one hundred percent vegetarian**. In the pristine state of Eden, God gave humanity fruits, seeds, grains, and nuts for sustenance. The archaic English word "meat" used in the King James Version of 1611 meant "solid nourishment" in general (just as the flesh of a coconut is still called "coconut meat"), not slaughtered animal carcasses.  
There was neither slaughterhouse nor bloodshed in the pristine kingdom of God. As the celebrated Biblical commentator **Rev. Dr. V.A. Holmes-Gore** observed: *"In Genesis 1:29, God's will regarding human diet is declared with absolute clarity. Plant food was the divine ideal; flesh-eating was only a later concession granted to fallen humanity after the Deluge, carrying with it the curse of fear and mutual dread."*

---

#### 12.3.2 The Sixth Commandment: Absolute Reverence for Life:

**Exodus 20:13 (The Decalogue / Ten Commandments)**

לֹא תִרְצָח׃

*Lo tirtsaḥ.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*lo* — you shall not / thou shalt not; *tirtsaḥ* — kill / slay / murder.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Thou shalt not kill."**

**PURPORT**  
This foundational divine commandment is stated with categorical brevity: *Lo tirtsaḥ*. Although modern translators often attempt to narrow the scope of this commandment to mean only the murder of a human being, the original ancient Hebrew verb *ratsaḥ* condemns all violent, unnecessary shedding of innocent life. When read in harmony with Genesis 1:29, the commandment stands as an absolute moral imperative: man has no authority to destroy the life that God has created.

---

#### 12.3.3 God's Boundless Mercy Encompasses All Creatures:

**Psalms 145:9 (Tehillim / The Book of Psalms)**

טֽוֹב־יְהוָ֥ה לַכֹּ֑ל וְ֝רַחֲמָ֗יו עַל־כָּל־מַעֲשָֽׂיו׃

*Tov-Adonai lakol; verakhamav al-kol-ma'asav.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*tov* — benevolent, good; *Adonai* — the Lord (YHWH); *lakol* — unto all; *verakhamav* — and His tender mercies and boundless compassion; *al-kol* — upon all; *ma'asav* — His works / His created beings.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"The Lord is good to all: and His tender mercies are over all His works."**

**PURPORT**  
The Psalmist King David clearly proclaims that God's loving kindness and compassion (*rakhamav*) are not restricted to human beings alone, but extend over *all* His works (*al-kol-ma'asav*)—encompassing every bird, animal, fish, and sentient creature. If God's tender mercies are bestowed upon every creature, how can any person claiming to love God ruthlessly slit the throats of those very creations merely to satisfy the tongue? True godliness demands reflecting the Almighty's universal mercy toward every living soul.

---

#### 12.3.4 Prophetic Denunciations of Animal Slaughter:

##### A. God Despises the Blood of Slaughtered Sacrifices:

**Isaiah 1:11 & 1:15**

לָמָּה־לִּי רֹב־זִבְחֵיכֶם יֹאמַר יְהוָה שָׂבַעְתִּי עֹלוֹת אֵילִים וְחֵלֶב מְרִיאִים וְדַם פָּרִים וּכְבָשִׂים וְעַתּוּדִים לֹא חָפָצְתִּי׃ ... וּבְפָרִשְׂכֶם כַּפֵּיכֶם אַעְלִים עֵינַי מִכֶּם גַּם כִּי־תַרְבּוּ תְפִלָּה אֵינֶנִּי שֹׁמֵעַ יְדֵיכֶם דָּמִים מָלֵאוּ׃

*Lammah-lli rov-zivkhekhem yomar Adonai? Sava'ti olot eylim vekhelev meri'im; vedam parim ukhvasim ve'attudim lo khafatsti... Uvfariskhem kappeikhem a'lim eynay mikkem; gam ki-tarbu tefillah eynenni shome'a; yedeikhem damim male'u.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*lammah-lli* — to what purpose to Me; *rov-zivkhekhem* — is the multitude of your slaughtered animal sacrifices; *yomar Adonai* — says the Lord; *sava'ti* — I am sated and disgusted; *olot eylim* — with the burnt offerings of rams; *vekhelev meri'im* — and the fat of fed beasts; *vedam parim* — and in the blood of bullocks; *ukhvasim* — or of lambs; *ve'attudim* — or of goats; *lo khafatsti* — I have no pleasure / I delight not (1:11)... *uvfariskhem* — and when you spread forth; *kappeikhem* — your hands in prayer; *a'lim* — I will hide; *eynay* — Mine eyes; *mikkem* — from you; *gam ki-tarbu* — yea, even when you multiply; *tefillah* — prayers; *eynenni shome'a* — I will not hear; *yedeikhem* — your hands; *damim* — with blood; *male'u* — are gorged and full! (1:15)

**TRANSLATION**  
**"'To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto Me?' saith the Lord: 'I am sated with the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he-goats... And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide Mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood!'"**

**PURPORT**  
Through the Prophet Isaiah, God forcefully rejects the hypocrisy of religious ceremonies accompanied by animal slaughter. The Almighty declares that He takes no pleasure in the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats. He warns that as long as human hands are stained with the blood of slaughtered animals (*yedeikhem damim male'u*), He will turn His eyes away and refuse to hear their prayers.

---

##### B. Equating Animal Slaughter to Manslaughter:

**Isaiah 66:3**

שׁוֹחֵט הַשּׁוֹר מַכֵּה־אִישׁ זוֹבֵחַ הַשֶּׂה עֹרֵף כֶּלֶב ...

*Shoḥet ha-shor makkeh-ish; zove'aḥ ha-seh oreif kelev...*

**SYNONYMS**  
*shoḥet* — he who slaughters; *ha-shor* — an ox; *makkeh-ish* — is as if he slew a human being; *zove'aḥ* — he who sacrifices; *ha-seh* — a lamb; *oreif* — is as if he breaks the neck of; *kelev* — a dog.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb is as if he broke a dog’s neck..."**

**PURPORT**  
In this striking verse, the Scripture directly equates the killing of an ox to the murder of a human being (*makkeh-ish*). In the eyes of divine cosmic justice, taking the life of an innocent, helpless creature of God is an act of violence indistinguishable from manslaughter.

---

#### 12.3.5 The Divine Botanical Economy: Fruit for Food, Leaves for Healing:

**Ezekiel 47:12 (Yechezkel / The Book of Ezekiel)**

וְעַל־הַנַּ֣חַל יַעֲלֶ֣ה עַל־שְׂפָת֣וֹ מִזֶּ֣ה ׀ וּמִזֶּ֣ה ׀ כָּל־עֵֽץ־מַ֠אֲכָל לֹא־יִבּ֨וֹל עָלֵ֜הוּ וְלֹֽא־יִתֹּ֣ם פִּרְי֗וֹ לָחֳדָשָׁיו֙ יְבַכֵּ֔ר כִּ֣י מֵימָ֔יו מִן־הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ הֵ֣מָּה יֽוֹצְאִ֑ים וְהָיָ֤ה פִרְיֹו֙ לְמַֽאֲכָ֔ל וְעָלֵ֖הוּ לִתְרוּפָֽה׃

*...ve'al-hannaḥal ya'aleh al-sefato mizzeh umizzeh kol-etz-ma'akhal lo-yibbol alehu velo-yittom piryo lekhodashav yevakker ki meymav min-hammiqdash hemmah yotze'im vehayah faryo le-ma'akhal ve'alehu litrufah.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*ve'al-hannaḥal* — and by the river; *ya'aleh* — shall grow; *al-sefato* — upon its bank; *mizzeh umizzeh* — on this side and on that side; *kol-etz-ma'akhal* — all trees for food; *lo-yibbol* — shall not wither; *alehu* — their leaf; *velo-yittom* — neither shall fail; *piryo* — their fruit; *lekhodashav* — according to its months; *yevakker* — it shall bring forth new fruit; *ki* — because; *meymav* — their waters; *min-hammiqdash* — from the sanctuary; *hemmah yotze'im* — they issue forth; *vehayah* — and shall be; *faryo* — the fruit thereof; *le-ma'akhal* — for food / sustenance; *ve'alehu* — and the leaf thereof; *litrufah* — for healing / medicine.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat [food], whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat [food], and the leaf thereof for medicine."**

**PURPORT**  
In this prophetic vision of the sanctified, redeemed world and the holy temple, the Prophet Ezekiel reveals that human life is designed by God to be nourished purely by the botanical kingdom. The fruits of the trees are designated as *le-ma'akhal* (food for sustenance) and their leaves as *litrufah* (for healing and medicine). There is no place for slaughterhouses, blood, or animal flesh in God's holy vision of health, life, and spiritual restoration.

---

#### 12.3.6 Linguistic Evidence in the Greek New Testament: Jesus Never Ate Meat:

Many Christians mistakenly assume that Jesus Christ ate animal flesh. A rigorous textual examination of the original **Koine Greek manuscripts** of the New Testament completely disproves this assumption:

##### 1. Mistranslation of General Greek Food Terms:

In the King James Bible and other early European translations, generic Greek words for food were repeatedly mistranslated into English as "meat":
\* **βρῶμα (*brōma*)** and **βρῶσις (*brōsis*)**: Derived from the verb *bibrōskō*, meaning simply "food," "nourishment," or "eating" (e.g., Romans 14:15, 1 Corinthians 8:8).
\* **τροφή (*trophē*)**: Derived from *trephō*, meaning "nourishment" or "sustenance" (e.g., Matthew 3:4, Acts 27:33).
\* **φαγεῖν (*phagein*)**: The infinitive of *esthiō*, meaning simply "to eat" or "to dine."

##### 2. The Total Absence of *Kreas* (Animal Flesh) in Connection with Jesus:

The explicit, exclusive Greek word for slaughtered animal flesh is **κρέας (*kreas*)**. Throughout the four Gospels, the word *kreas* is **never once used** in connection with Jesus Christ eating!

##### 3. Apostolic Commands to Abstain from Meat:

**Romans 14:21 (The Epistles of Paul - Koine Greek)**

καλὸν τὸ μὴ φαγεῖν κρέα μηδὲ πιεῖν οἶνον μηδὲ ἐν ᾧ ὁ ἀδελφός σου προσκόπτει ἢ σκανדαλίζεται ἢ ἀσθενεῖ.

*Kalon to mē phagein krea mēde piein oinon, mēde en hō ho adelphos sou proskoptei, ē skandalizetai, ē asthenei.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*kalon* — good, noble, morally upright; *to mē phagein* — not to eat; *krea* — animal flesh (meat); *mēde* — neither; *piein* — to drink; *oinon* — wine; *mēde* — nor; *en hō* — anything whereby; *ho adelphos sou* — your brother; *proskoptei* — stumbles; *ē* — or; *skandalizetai* — is offended; *ē asthenei* — or is made weak.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor any thing whereby thy brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak."**

**PURPORT**  
Here the Apostle Paul explicitly uses the unambiguous Greek word **κρέας (*kreas*)**, which strictly denotes animal flesh, distinguished from generic foods (*brōma* or *trophē*). The unequivocal apostolic instruction is that abstaining from animal flesh (*mē phagein krea*) and intoxicating wine (*mēde piein oinon*) is spiritually good, righteous, and noble (*kalon*).

---

**1 Corinthians 8:13 (The Epistles of Paul - Koine Greek)**

διόπερ εἰ βρῶμα σκανדαλίζει τὸν ἀδελφόν μου, οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἵνα μὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν μου σκανדαλίσω.

*Dioper ei brōma skandalizei ton adelphon mou, ou mē phagō krea eis ton aiōna, hina mē ton adelphon mou skandalisō.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*dioper* — wherefore, therefore; *ei* — if; *brōma* — food; *skandalizei* — causes to stumble / offends; *ton adelphon mou* — my brother; *ou mē phagō* — I will never eat / by no means will I eat; *krea* — animal flesh; *eis ton aiōna* — unto eternity / for evermore; *hina mē* — so that not; *ton adelphon mou* — my brother; *skandalisō* — I should cause to stumble.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Wherefore, if meat [food] make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth, lest I make my brother to offend."**

**PURPORT**  
In this foundational passage, the Apostle Paul makes a clear and deliberate linguistic distinction: while generic food is referred to as *brōma*, when speaking of slaughtered animal flesh, he deliberately shifts to the precise term **κρέα (*krea*)**. He solemnly declares that he will never consume animal flesh for all eternity (*ou mē phagō krea eis ton aiōna*), establishing that abstaining from flesh-eating is the hallmark of true spiritual consideration and holiness.

---

##### 4. Historical Records of the Apostles and Early Church Fathers:

Authentic historical documents preserved by early Christian historians confirm that the Apostles and early followers of Christ were strict vegetarians:
\* **St. Jerome (Translator of the Latin Vulgate, 4th Century):**

> *"The eating of animal flesh was unknown until the deluge; but since the deluge, the dregs and stink of animal flesh have been stuffed into our mouths... Jesus Christ, who appeared when the time was fulfilled, brought the end back to the beginning, so that we are no longer permitted to eat animal flesh."*  
> *(Adversus Jovinianum 1.30)*
> \* **Eusebius of Caesarea (Father of Church History, 3rd Century):** Records in his *Ecclesiastical History* that **St. James the Just** (the brother of the Lord and head of the Jerusalem Church) never tasted animal flesh or wine, wore simple linen garments, and spent his life in prayer.
> \* **Clement of Alexandria (2nd Century):** Records in *Paedagogus* (II.1):  
> *"It is far better to be happy than to make our bodies the tombstones of dead beasts. The Apostle Matthew partook of seeds, nuts, and vegetables, without flesh."*
> \* **The Nazarenes and Ebionites:** The earliest Jewish-Christian disciples of Jesus, the Nazarenes, strictly adhered to a vegetarian diet, following the original commandment of Eden (Genesis 1:29). Jesus identified Himself with the Nazarenes, confirming His rejection of meat.

---

fields.subTopic: The Buddha’s Uncompromising Rejection of Meat: Analysis of the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra and Dhammapada
fields.article:
### 12.4 Principles of Buddhism:

The entire edifice of Buddhism rests upon the bedrock of *Ahiṁsā* (universal non-violence) and *Karuṇā* (boundless compassion for all sentient life). When humanity degenerated into rampant animal slaughter under the distorted pretext of Vedic rituals, Lord Buddha descended to deliver fallen souls from the catastrophic karma of slaughterhouses, teaching that no spiritual enlightenment is possible while participating in the shedding of innocent blood.

---

#### 12.4.1 Universal Empathy: Comparing All Beings to Oneself:

**Dhammapada, Verse 129 (Daṇḍavagga / Chapter on Punishment)**

सब्बे तसन्ति दण्डस्स सब्बे भायन्ति मच्चुनो।  
अत्तानं उपमं कत्वा न हनेय्य न घातये॥

*Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbe bhāyanti maccuno;*  
*Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*sabbe* — all living beings; *tasanti* — tremble, shudder in terror; *daṇḍassa* — of punishment, weapon, violence; *sabbe* — all creatures; *bhāyanti* — fear, are terrified; *maccuno* — of death; *attānaṁ* — oneself; *upamaṁ katvā* — comparing, putting oneself in another's place; *na* — not; *haneyya* — one should strike or kill; *na* — nor; *ghātaye* — should cause others to kill.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"All living beings tremble before violence; all creatures fear death. Putting oneself in the place of another, one should neither kill nor cause another to kill."**

**PURPORT**  
In this foundational verse of the *Dhammapada*, Lord Buddha establishes the universal golden rule of non-violence through intuitive psychological empathy. Every sentient being—from the smallest insect to the largest cow, pig, or sheep—cherishes its own life and desperately flees from suffering and extermination. When animals are dragged into the slaughterhouse, their trembling limbs, desperate cries, and terror-stricken eyes prove beyond doubt that they value their lives as dearly as any human being values his own.  
Lord Buddha therefore commands: *attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā*—put yourself in the animal's place! If you would scream in agony and terror if a butcher held a knife to your throat, how can you inflict that exact horror upon an innocent animal? Furthermore, the injunction *na haneyya na ghātaye* is categorical: one must neither strike the blow oneself nor cause another to kill by purchasing the carcass. The consumer who buys meat in the market is directly responsible for causing the slaughter (*ghātaye*).

---

#### 12.4.2 The Karmic Law: No Happiness for the Tormenter of Beings:

**Dhammapada, Verse 131 (Daṇḍavagga / Chapter on Punishment)**

सुखकामानि भूतानि यो दण्डेन विहिंसति।  
अत्तनो सुखमेसानो पेच्च सो न लभते सुखं॥

*Sukha-kāmāni bhūtāni, yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati;*  
*Attano sukham-esāno, pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*sukha-kāmāni* — yearning for happiness, desiring pleasure and peace; *bhūtāni* — living beings, creatures; *yo* — whoever; *daṇḍena* — with a weapon, rod, or violence; *vihiṁsati* — torments, harms, or slaughters; *attano* — his own; *sukham* — pleasure, gratification; *esāno* — seeking, desiring; *pecca* — after death, in the next life; *so* — that person; *na* — never; *labhate* — attains; *sukhaṁ* — happiness or peace.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Whoever, seeking his own happiness, harms or slaughters with a rod living creatures who also yearn for happiness, will not attain happiness after death."**

**PURPORT**  
The law of *karma* operates with mathematical precision. Every living creature (*bhūtāni*) shares the identical existential desire: to be free from pain and to experience happiness (*sukha-kāmāni*). When an individual seeks to gratify his own tongue and palate (*attano sukham-esāno*) by destroying the life of an innocent animal, he sows seeds of excruciating suffering. Lord Buddha warns that whoever causes misery to other living beings will find that all happiness vanishes from his life; after death (*pecca*), he is dragged into hellish realms of retribution where he must repay every agony he inflicted.

---

#### 12.4.3 Definition of a True Noble Person (*Ariya*):

**Dhammapada, Verse 270 (Dhammatthavagga / The Righteous)**

न तेन अरियो होति येन पाणानि हिंसति।  
अहिंसा सब्बपाणानं ‘अरियो’ति पवुच्चति॥

*Na tena ariyo hoti, yena pāṇāni hiṁsati;*  
*Ahiṁsā sabba-pāṇānaṁ, 'ariyo'ti pavuccati.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*na* — not; *tena* — by that; *ariyo* — a noble person, holy person (Aryan); *hoti* — becomes; *yena* — by which; *pāṇāni* — living beings with breath; *hiṁsati* — one harms, injures, or slaughters; *ahiṁsā* — non-violence, harmlessness, compassion; *sabba-pāṇānaṁ* — toward all living creatures; *ariyo* — noble; *iti* — thus; *pavuccati* — he is called.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"A man is not noble because he injures or slaughters living creatures. By practicing harmlessness and compassion toward all living beings, one is truly called noble [ariyo]."**

**PURPORT**  
In the ancient culture of Bhārata-varṣa, the title *Ārya* (Pali: *Ariya*) denoted a person of sublime moral nobility and spiritual enlightenment. Lord Buddha decisively clarifies that one does not become noble through family pedigree, erudition, or outward social standing while participating in the slaughter of living beings (*yena pāṇāni hiṁsati*). Real nobility is defined solely by *ahiṁsā sabba-pāṇānaṁ*—universal, unconditional compassion extended to all beings endowed with the breath of life (*pāṇa*). A person who eats meat or supports animal slaughter is spiritually ignoble, regardless of his secular achievements.

---

#### 12.4.4 The Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra: The Buddha's Uncompromising Rejection of Meat:

The *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*—one of the most authoritative Mahāyāna Buddhist scriptures—contains an entire chapter exclusively dedicated to the total prohibition of meat-eating, entitled **Māṁsa-bhakṣaṇa-parivarta (Discourse on Meat-Eating)**. In this scripture, the Bodhisattva Mahāmati questions the Buddha:

**Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter 8, Verse 1**

मद्यमांसपलाण्डूनां भक्षणे दोषकीर्तनम्।  
सर्वबुद्धसुतानां च ब्रूहि मे धर्मनायक॥

*Madya-māṁsa-palāṇḍūnāṁ bhakṣaṇe doṣa-kīrtanam;*  
*Sarva-buddha-sutānāṁ ca brūhi me dharmanāyaka.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*madya* — alcohol, intoxicating drink; *māṁsa* — animal flesh, meat; *palāṇḍūnāṁ* — onions and garlic; *bhakṣaṇe* — in the eating and consumption of; *doṣa* — the grave evils, moral pollution, karmic faults; *kīrtanam* — enumeration, proclamation; *sarva-buddha-sutānāṁ* — for all the sons and disciples of the Buddha (Bodhisattvas); *ca* — and; *brūhi* — please declare; *me* — unto me; *dharmanāyaka* — O supreme Guide and Leader of Dharma!

**TRANSLATION**  
**"The Bodhisattva Mahāmati addressed the Blessed One: 'O Leader of Dharma! Please declare unto us the grave moral evils and karmic pollutions resulting from the consumption of intoxicating drink, animal flesh, onions, and garlic, for the guidance of all the sons of the Buddha [Bodhisattvas].'"**

---

##### A. All Animals Were Once Our Mothers and Fathers:

**Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter 8**

अनन्तभवपरम्परायां महामते नास्त्यसौ कश्चित्सत्त्वो यो न माता बभूव पिता वा भ्राता वा भगिनी वा पुत्रो वा दुहिता वा। तत्कथं बोधिसत्त्वः सर्वसत्त्वेषु आत्मसंज्ञी सन् मांसं भक्षयेत्॥

*Ananta-bhava-paramparāyāṁ mahāmate nasty-asau kaścit-sattvo yo na mātā babhūva pitā vā bhrātā vā bhaginī vā putro vā duhitā vā; tat-kathaṁ bodhisattvaḥ sarva-sattveṣu ātma-saṁjñī san māṁsaṁ bhakṣayet.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*ananta-bhava-paramparāyāṁ* — in the beginningless cycle of transmigrations and reincarnations; *mahāmate* — O great-minded Mahāmati; *na asti asau kaścit* — there is not any single; *sattvaḥ* — sentient creature, animal; *yaḥ* — who; *na* — not; *mātā babhūva* — has been one's mother; *pitā vā* — or one's father; *bhrātā vā* — or one's brother; *bhaginī vā* — or one's sister; *putro vā* — or one's son; *duhitā vā* — or one's daughter; *tat-katham* — how then; *bodhisattvaḥ* — a compassionate seeker of enlightenment; *sarva-sattveṣu* — toward all living beings; *ātma-saṁjñī san* — recognizing them as his own self and family; *māṁsaṁ* — meat, animal flesh; *bhakṣayet* — could consume?

**TRANSLATION**  
**"In the beginningless and endless cycle of reincarnation, O Mahāmati, there is not a single living creature who has not once been your mother, your father, your brother, your sister, your son, or your daughter! Transmigrating through various species, they are reborn as cows, sheep, birds, and fish. How then can a compassionate spiritual seeker, who recognizes all creatures as his kin, devour the flesh of his own kin?"**

**PURPORT**  
Here Lord Buddha reveals the profound truth of reincarnation (*saṁsāra*). In the transmigratory journey of the soul through 8,400,000 species of life, every living entity has been related to every other entity in countless past incarnations. The animal being dragged to the abattoir today was once one's caring mother or beloved child in a former birth. Devouring animal flesh is therefore nothing less than consuming the flesh of one's own family members. A person who realizes this cosmic reality can never partake of animal flesh without horror and revulsion.

---

##### B. Meat-Eating is Unconditionally Prohibited Forever:

**Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, Chapter 8**

नैव मया कस्यचिन्मांसमनुज्ञातं नानुजानामि नानुज्ञास्यामि। सर्वथा सर्वदा सर्वत्र सर्वथा निषिद्धम्॥

*Naiva mayā kasyacin-māṁsam anujñātaṁ, nānujānāmi, nānujñāsyāmi; sarvathā sarvadā sarvatra sarvathā niṣiddham.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*na eva* — never indeed; *mayā* — by Me (the Buddha); *kasyacit* — to anyone whatsoever; *māṁsam* — consumption of animal flesh; *anujñātam* — was permitted or authorized; *na anujānāmi* — nor do I permit it now; *na anujñāsyāmi* — nor will I ever permit it in the future; *sarvathā* — in every way; *sarvadā* — at all times; *sarvatra* — in every place; *sarvathā* — under all circumstances; *niṣiddham* — strictly forbidden and prohibited.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"I have never permitted meat-eating to anyone, I do not permit it now, and I will never permit it in the future! In every way, at all times, in every place, and under all circumstances, meat-eating is unconditionally prohibited for all who follow the spiritual path."**

**PURPORT**  
Modern meat-eaters sometimes try to justify their habit by fabricating myths that the Buddha allowed meat under certain conditions (such as the so-called "threefold purity"). In this unequivocal declaration from the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*, the Buddha obliterates every such compromise: *Naiva mayā kasyacin-māṁsam anujñātaṁ*—"I have never permitted it to anyone, I do not permit it now, and I shall never permit it!" The Buddha explicitly declares that meat-eating produces noxious bodily odors, destroys the capacity for meditation, creates terrifying nightmares, terrifies wild animals, and binds the soul to the lower realms of misery.

---

#### 12.4.5 The Vedic Perspective on Lord Buddha's Mission:

Vedic scriptures confirm that Lord Buddha is an empowered incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who appeared specifically to stop the massacre of innocent animals:

**Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (1.3.24)**

ततः कलौ सम्प्रवृत्ते सम्मोहाय सुरद्विषाम्।  
बुद्धो नाम्नाञ्जनसुतः कीकटेषु भविष्यति॥

*tataḥ kalau sampravṛtte sammohāya sura-dviṣām*  
*buddho nāmnāñjana-sutaḥ kīkaṭeṣu bhaviṣyati*

**SYNONYMS**  
*tataḥ* — thereafter; *kalau* — the Age of Kali; *sampravṛtte* — having commenced; *sammohāya* — for bewildering and subduing; *sura-dviṣām* — the envious enemies of the devotees (demons); *buddhaḥ* — Lord Buddha; *nāmnā* — by the name; *añjana-sutaḥ* — the son of Añjanā; *kīkaṭeṣu* — in the province of Gayā (Bihar); *bhaviṣyati* — will take birth.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Then, in the beginning of the Age of Kali, the Supreme Lord will appear as Lord Buddha, the son of Añjanā, in the province of Gayā [Bihar], for the purpose of bewildering those who are envious of the faithful devotees."**

**Śrīla Jayadeva Gosvāmī's Gīta-govinda (Daśāvatāra-stotra, Verse 9)**

निन्दसि यज्ञविधेरहह श्रुतिजातं  
सदयहृदय दर्शितपशुघातम्।  
केशव धृतबुद्धशरीर जय जगदीश हरे॥

*Nindasi yajña-vidher ahaha śruti-jātaṁ*  
*Sadaya-hṛdaya darśita-paśu-ghātam*  
*Keśava dhṛta-buddha-śarīra jaya jagadīśa hare!*

**SYNONYMS**  
*nindasi* — You decry, criticize, and reject; *yajña-vidheḥ* — of the sacrificial rituals; *ahaha* — alas; *śruti-jātam* — the Vedic scriptural injunctions; *sadaya-hṛdaya* — O Lord of compassionate and merciful heart; *darśita-paśu-ghātam* — seeing the gruesome slaughter of animals; *keśava* — O Lord Keśava, slayer of the Keśī demon; *dhṛta-buddha-śarīra* — who have assumed the divine transcendental form of Buddha; *jaya* — all glories to You; *jagad-īśa* — O Supreme Lord of the universe; *hare* — O Lord Hari!

**TRANSLATION**  
**"O Lord Keśava! O Lord of the universe! O Lord Hari, who have assumed the form of Buddha! All glories to You! O Buddha of boundless compassionate heart, You decried and rejected the Vedic sacrificial rituals because You could not bear to witness the gruesome slaughter of poor, innocent animals performed under the false shelter of the Vedas!"**

**PURPORT BY ŚRĪLA PRABHUPĀDA**  
In his purports to *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* and *Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta*, His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda explains the divine purpose of Lord Buddha's advent:  
When the degraded people of Kali-yuga took advantage of certain Vedic concessions to open slaughterhouses and murder animals under the nominal pretext of "Vedic sacrifice" (*yajña*), the Supreme Lord appeared as Gautama Buddha. Seeing the terrifying cruelty inflicted upon dumb animals, the Lord's heart melted with compassion (*sadaya-hṛdaya darśita-paśu-ghātam*). In order to establish *ahiṁsā* (non-violence) as the supreme principle, Lord Buddha ostensibly rejected the authority of the Vedas, declaring: *"I do not accept your Vedic scriptures if they justify the slaughter of innocent animals!"*  
Lord Buddha did this because the fallen, meat-addicted population was misinterpreting Vedic verses to justify their bloodlust. By preaching absolute non-violence (*ahiṁsā paramo dharmaḥ*), Lord Buddha saved the poor animals from the slaughterhouse and saved human beings from the catastrophic karmic reactions of animal killing.

---

fields.subTopic: Ahiṁsā as Supreme Religion in Jainism: The 108 Mathematical Dimensions of Non-Violence
fields.article:
### 12.5 Principles of Jainism:

In the sacred tradition of Jainism, *Ahiṁsā* (universal non-violence) is not merely a moral virtue, but the supreme spiritual reality and absolute condition for the liberation of the soul (*mokṣa*): **अहिंसा परमो धर्मः (*Ahiṁsā paramo dharmaḥ*)**. Jain philosophy recognizes every living entity—from microscopic organisms to animals and human beings—as an eternal conscious soul (*jīva*) endowed with intrinsic spiritual purity and the capacity for suffering. In this rigorous tradition, slaughtering animals for food or partaking of animal flesh is regarded as the most abhorrent and spiritually catastrophic sin.

---

#### 12.5.1 The Universal Soul Axiom: The Jain Cosmic Motto:

**Tattvārtha Sūtra (5.21 - Ācārya Umāsvāti)**

परस्परोपग्रहो जीवानाम्॥

*Parasparopagraho jīvānām.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*paraspara* — mutually, of one another; *upagrahaḥ* — rendering service, mutual support, protection, and assistance; *jīvānām* — of all living souls.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"All living souls are bound together in mutual interdependence, ordained to assist, protect, and support one another."**

**PURPORT**  
This ancient sūtra by Ācārya Umāsvāti is the universally revered emblem of Jainism. It affirms that the cosmic order is designed for mutual preservation and cooperative coexistence, not violent predation. Endowed with higher cognitive faculties, human beings have a sacred obligation to extend protection (*upagraha*) to the weaker, voiceless animal kingdom. To exploit, torture, and slaughter innocent animals for the momentary pleasure of the palate is an egregious violation of the universal cosmic contract.

---

#### 12.5.2 The Philosophical Definition of *Hiṁsā* (Violence):

**Tattvārtha Sūtra (7.18 / 7.22 - Ācārya Umāsvāti)**

प्रमत्तयोगात्प्राणव्यपरोपणं हिंसा॥

*Pramatta-yogāt prāṇa-vyaparopaṇaṁ hiṁsā.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*pramatta-yogāt* — from negligent, careless, or passion-driven activity of mind, body, and speech; *prāṇa* — the vital life-forces or sensory faculties of a living being; *vyaparopaṇam* — severing, destroying, or taking away; *hiṁsā* — is defined as violence.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"The severance or destruction of the vital life-forces [prāṇa] of any living creature due to careless, passion-driven, or negligent activity of mind, body, or speech is defined as violence [hiṁsā]."**

**PURPORT**  
Jain ontology defines violence with profound precision: *hiṁsā* is any action wherein life-forces (*prāṇa*) are extinguished through *pramāda*—spiritual negligence, heedlessness, or passion-driven indulgence. In meat-eating, both criteria are fully present:  
1. The animal's life-forces (physical body, breath, senses, and consciousness) are violently destroyed (*prāṇa-vyaparopaṇam*).  
2. The act is motivated entirely by *pramāda*—the unbridled passion and sensory addiction (*lobha*) of the human tongue.  
Therefore, the consumption of meat constitutes blatant, unmitigated *hiṁsā*.

---

#### 12.5.3 Universal Cherishing of Life: The Cry of All Creatures:

**Ācārāṅga Sūtra (Book 1, Chapter 2, Lesson 3 / 1.5.5 - Words of Bhagavān Mahāvīra)**

सव्वे पाणा पियाउया सुहसाया दुक्खपडिकूला अप्पियवहा पियजीविणो जीविउकामा,  
सव्वेसिं जीवियं पियं।

*Savve pāṇā piyāuyā suha-sāyā dukkha-paḍikūlā appiya-vahā piya-jīviṇo jīviu-kāmā,*  
*savvesiṁ jīviyaṁ piyaṁ.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*savve* — all; *pāṇā* — living creatures endowed with breath; *piyāuyā* — love and cherish their own lifespan; *suha-sāyā* — yearn for joy, comfort, and peace; *dukkha-paḍikūlā* — are averse to and recoil from pain and suffering; *appiya-vahā* — abhor destruction, slaughter, and death; *piya-jīviṇo* — love their very existence; *jīviu-kāmā* — long to continue living; *savvesiṁ* — unto every single being; *jīviyaṁ* — life; *piyaṁ* — is dearly cherished and beloved.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"All living creatures love life; they yearn for comfort and joy, and recoil with terror from pain and agony. They abhor slaughter, they love to live, and they long to continue existing. To every single living being, its own life is immensely precious and beloved!"**

**PURPORT**  
In this celebrated passage from the *Ācārāṅga Sūtra*, Bhagavān Mahāvīra articulates the heart of animal psychology. No bird, fish, cow, or sheep volunteers to enter the slaughterhouse. Every animal struggles frantically against the butcher’s rope, cries out in terror, and seeks desperately to preserve its life. Life is as precious to an animal as it is to a human mother or child. To brutally sever an animal's existence merely to chew upon its muscular tissues is a display of demonic cruelty.

---

#### 12.5.4 "Thou Art That": Inflicting Pain on Another is Harming Oneself:

**Ācārāṅga Sūtra (Book 1, Chapter 5, Lesson 5)**

तं चेव हंतव्वं मंनसि, जं हंतव्वं मंनसि तं चेव अत्ता।  
जं दण्डवेत्तव्वं मंनसि, तं चेव अत्ता॥

*Taṁ ceva hantavvaṁ mannasi, jaṁ hantavvaṁ mannasi taṁ ceva attā;*  
*Jaṁ daṇḍavettavvaṁ mannasi, taṁ ceva attā.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*taṁ ceva* — that very creature; *hantavvaṁ* — worthy to be slaughtered or killed; *mannasi* — you imagine or deem; *jaṁ* — whom; *hantavvaṁ mannasi* — you consider fit to slay; *taṁ ceva* — that very being is; *attā* — your own self; *jaṁ* — whom; *daṇḍavettavvaṁ* — fit to be struck, tortured, or punished; *mannasi* — you consider; *taṁ ceva* — that very being is; *attā* — your own self.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"The creature whom you deem fit to slaughter is none other than your own self! The creature whom you consider fit to strike, torment, and punish is none other than your own self!"**

**PURPORT**  
This is the sublime metaphysical principle of Jain non-dual compassion (*ātmatulya-dṛṣṭi*): treating all beings as one's very own self. The soul residing in the body of an animal is identical in spiritual essence to the soul residing in a human body. When one strikes an animal, one strikes oneself. When one slaughters a creature, one commits spiritual suicide. By the immutable law of karma, the agonizing pain inflicted upon the victim rebounds upon the tormentor in exact equal measure.

---

#### 12.5.5 The Scientific Impossibility of Meat Without Violence:

**Puruṣārthasiddhyupāya (Verses 65 & 67 - Ācārya Amṛtacandra Sūri)**

न विना प्राणविघातान्मांसस्योत्पत्तिरिष्यते यस्मात्।  
मांसं भजतः प्रसवत्यनभ्युपेतापि तद्धिंसा॥  
यत्किञ्चित्पिशितं तत्सर्वं सचित्तनिचितमेव।  
तत्र भवत्येव सदा सूक्ष्मजीवप्रघातोऽपि॥

*Na vinā prāṇa-vighātān māṁsasyotpattir iṣyate yasmāt;*  
*Māṁsaṁ bhajataḥ prasavaty-anabhyupetāpi tad-dhiṁsā.*  
*Yat-kiñcit piśitaṁ tat sarvaṁ sacitta-nicitam eva;*  
*Tatra bhavaty eva sadā sūkṣma-jīva-praghāto 'pi.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*na vinā* — never without; *prāṇa-vighātāt* — the violent destruction and slaughter of living beings; *māṁsasya* — of animal flesh, meat; *utpattiḥ* — the production or procurement; *iṣyate* — is possible; *yasmāt* — because; *māṁsaṁ bhajataḥ* — to him who partakes of or consumes meat; *prasavati* — accrues, is generated; *anabhyupetā api* — even if not directly slaughtered with his own hands; *tat-hiṁsā* — that terrible violence; *yat-kiñcit* — whatever; *piśitam* — cut of animal flesh; *tat sarvaṁ* — all of that; *sacitta-nicitam eva* — is a dense breeding ground of innumerable micro-organisms; *tatra* — therein; *bhavati eva* — occurs constantly; *sadā* — always; *sūkṣma-jīva* — of microscopic living beings; *praghātaḥ api* — continuous destruction.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Because meat can never be produced without the violent destruction of living beings, whoever consumes flesh is inevitably guilty of that slaughter, even if the killing was done by someone else! Furthermore, every cut of flesh is a decaying breeding ground teeming with millions of microscopic organisms; whoever partakes of meat continuously slaughters countless living souls with every single bite."**

**PURPORT**  
Ācārya Amṛtacandra Sūri thoroughly refutes the false rationalization of modern consumers who claim: *"I did not kill the animal; the slaughterhouse butcher did."* Without the consumer who buys the carcass, the butcher would never strike the blade. By paying money for meat, the consumer hires the butcher to commit murder on his behalf.  
Furthermore, Jain biology reveals that dead flesh undergoes immediate decay, generating colonies of microscopic sentient life (*nigoda / sūkṣma-jīva*). Therefore, the meat-eater is doubly condemned: he bears the guilt of the slaughtered mammal, and he annihilates millions of micro-organisms within his mouth and digestive tract.

---

#### 12.5.6 The 108 Mathematical Dimensions of Hiṁsā:

Jain philosophy categorizes **108 distinct avenues** through which the sin of violence binds the soul in catastrophic karma, calculated by the mathematical permutations of action:

\text{Total Avenues of Karma} = 3 \text{ Modes} \times 3 \text{ Mediums} \times 4 \text{ Passions} \times 3 \text{ Phases} = 108

1. **The Three Modes of Action (*Karaṇa*):**  
   \* **Kṛta:** Directly killing the animal oneself.  
   \* **Kārita:** Causing someone else to kill (e.g., purchasing meat from a butcher, thereby financing and commanding the slaughter).  
   \* **Anumodita:** Approving, consenting to, or rejoicing in the killing of animals.
2. **The Three Mediums of Execution (*Yoga*):**  
   \* **Mana:** Harboring violent thoughts, cravings, or desires in the mind.  
   \* **Vacana:** Speaking words that encourage, justify, or praise meat-eating.  
   \* **Kāya:** Physical bodily actions (buying, cooking, chewing, and digesting flesh).
3. **The Four Deep-Rooted Passions (*Kaṣāya*):**  
   \* **Krodha:** Violence born of anger or aggression.  
   \* **Māna:** Violence born of pride, vanity, or social status.  
   \* **Māyā:** Violence born of deceit and hypocritical excuses.  
   \* **Lobha:** Violence born of uncontrolled greed and sensory tongue-addiction.
4. **The Three Phases of Manifestation:**  
   \* **Samārambha:** Conceiving and planning the violent act.  
   \* **Samārambha / Samudyama:** Preparing the instruments, ingredients, and finances for slaughter.  
   \* **Ārambha:** The final physical execution and consumption.

Because every meat-eater commits violence through *Kārita* (causing another to slaughter), through *Kāya* and *Vacana*, driven by *Lobha* (tongue greed), through all three phases of consumption, he incurs massive, unyielding karmic bondage across all 108 avenues simultaneously.

---

#### 12.5.7 The Supreme Compassion of Tīrthaṅkara Neminātha:

The historic life of **Lord Neminātha** (the 22nd Tīrthaṅkara) stands as one of the most powerful testimonies against meat-eating in world literature (*Uttarādhyayana Sūtra*):  
On the joyous day of His royal wedding, Prince Neminātha was riding in a royal chariot toward the palace of His bride, Princess Rājīmatī. Along the pathway, He heard agonizing, heart-rending screams and wailing. Looking into large wooden pens, He saw thousands of terrified deer, antelopes, peacocks, cattle, and sheep packed tightly, trembling in cold terror.  
When Prince Neminātha inquired why these innocent creatures were confined, His charioteer replied:

> *"O Prince, these animals are gathered to be slaughtered today so that their flesh may be cooked to feast the royal guests at Your wedding banquet!"*

Upon hearing that his wedding celebration was to be consecrated with the blood and agony of innocent animals, Neminātha's heart was pierced with intolerable grief. He immediately ordered: *"Open the gates and set every single animal free!"*  
On the spot, Prince Neminātha removed His royal ornaments, cancelled His wedding, renounced His kingdom, and walked away into the Girnar mountains to embrace lifelong asceticism and proclaim universal compassion (*Ahiṁsā*). He declared that a life built upon the cries of slaughtered creatures is a curse, and that true spiritual royalty lies in protecting all life.

---

fields.subTopic: Meat Prohibition in Sikhism: Guru Nanak, Bhagat Kabir, and the Pure Tradition of Guru-kā-Langar
fields.article:
### 12.6 Principles of Sikhism and the Sacred Tradition of Guru-kā-Langar:

The sacred scriptures of Sikhism—enshrined in the **Guru Granth Sahib Ji**—proclaim that the supreme Lord (*Ikk Oaṅkār*) permeates every atom of the cosmos, residing in the hearts of all living beings. Cruelty to animals, the consumption of carcasses, and the hypocritical slaughter of innocent creatures under religious pretenses are denounced with uncompromising moral clarity by the Sikh Gurus and Bhagats.

---

#### 12.6.1 Bhagat Kabir Ji: Hypocrisy of Ritual Slaughter and Tongue-Lust:

**Guru Granth Sahib Ji (Ang 1374, Salok 135 - Bhagat Kabir Ji)**

ਕਬੀਰ ਬੇਦ ਕਤੇਬ ਕਹਹੁ ਮਤ ਝੂਠੇ ਝੂਠਾ ਜੋ ਨ ਬਿਚਾਰੈ ॥  
ਜਉ ਸਭ ਮਹਿ ਏਕੁ ਖੁਦਾਇ ਰਹਤ ਹੈ ਤਉ ਕਿਉ ਮੁਰਗੀ ਮਾਰੈ ॥੧੩੫॥

*Kabīr bed kateb kahahu mat jhūṭhe, jhūṭhā jo na bicārai;*  
*Jau sabh mahi eku khudāi rahat hai, tau kiu murgī mārai.* (135)

**SYNONYMS**  
*kabīr* — O Kabir; *bed* — the Vedic scriptures; *kateb* — the Semitic scriptures (Torah, Psalms, Gospel, Quran); *kahahu mat jhūṭhe* — do not call false or untrue; *jhūṭhā* — false and blind is he; *jo* — who; *na bicārai* — does not contemplate or understand their true spiritual essence; *jau* — since, if; *sabh mahi* — within all living creatures; *eku khudāi* — the one Supreme Creator (Allah / God); *rahat hai* — abides, dwells; *tau* — then; *kiu* — why; *murgī mārai* — do you violently butcher a chicken?

**TRANSLATION**  
**"O Kabir! Do not brand the holy scriptures as false; false is that person who does not contemplate their true divine essence! If you profess that the one Supreme Lord dwells within all living beings, why then do you violently butcher a chicken for the gratification of your tongue?"**

**PURPORT**  
Bhagat Kabir Ji exposes the glaring spiritual hypocrisy of those who recite sacred scriptures while continuing to participate in the slaughter of innocent creatures. If God is omnipresent and dwells within all living entities as the indwelling Witness (*Antaryāmī*), then severing the throat of a bird or animal is an assault upon God's temple. Kabir asks with razor-sharp logic: How can any man claim to revere the Almighty while shedding the blood of the Almighty's own helpless children?

---

#### 12.6.2 Denunciation of Slaughter Disguised as Religion:

**Guru Granth Sahib Ji (Ang 1377, Salok 187 - Bhagat Kabir Ji)**

ਕਬੀਰ ਜੀਆ ਬਧਹੁ ਸੁ ਧਰਮੁ ਕਰਿ ਥਾਪਹੁ ਕਹੁ ਧਰਮੁ ਕਹੁ ਕੈਸਾ ॥  
ਆਪਨ ਕਉ ਮੁਨੀਵਰ ਕਰਿ ਥਾਪਹੁ ਕਾ ਕਉ ਕਹਹੁ ਕਸਾਈ ॥੧੮੭॥

*Kabīr jīā badhahu su dharamu kari thāpahu, kahu dharamu kahu kaisā;*  
*Āpan kau munīvar kari thāpahu, kā kau kahahu kasāī.* (187)

**SYNONYMS**  
*kabīr* — O Kabir; *jīā badhahu* — you slaughter and murder living creatures; *su* — and that very act; *dharamu kari thāpahu* — you sanctimoniously establish and declare as religious duty (dharma); *kahu* — tell me; *dharamu* — religion; *kahu kaisā* — what kind of religion is this?; *āpan kau* — unto yourself; *munīvar kari thāpahu* — you proclaim yourself to be a noble sage, priest, or holy person; *kā kau* — whom on earth; *kahahu* — would you then call; *kasāī* — a butcher?

**TRANSLATION**  
**"O Kabir! You ruthlessly slaughter living beings and proclaim it to be an act of religion! Tell me, what kind of 'religion' is this? If you consider yourself a saintly sage while slaughtering helpless creatures, then tell me: whom on earth would you call a butcher?"**

**PURPORT**  
In this devastating verse, Bhagat Kabir shatters the rationalizations of priests, clerics, and ritualists who butcher animals in the name of God. To inflict agony and death upon a defenseless animal and call it "dharma" or "religious duty" is the absolute perversion of spirituality. Kabir declares that anyone who cuts the throat of an animal is fundamentally a butcher (*kasāī*), regardless of the robes, titles, or religious rituals he hides behind.

---

#### 12.6.3 Guru Nanak Dev Ji: Usurping Life is Like Eating Carrion:

**Guru Granth Sahib Ji (Ang 141, Mājhkī Vār - Guru Nanak Dev Ji)**

ਹਕੁ ਪਰਾਇਆ ਨਾਨਕਾ ਉਸੁ ਸੂਅਰ ਉਸੁ ਗਾਇ ॥  
ਗੁਰੁ ਪੀਰੁ ਹਾਮਾ ਤਾ ਭਰੇ ਜਾ ਮੁਰਦਾਰੁ ਨ ਖਾਇ ॥

*Haku parāiā Nānakā usu sūaru usu gāi;*  
*Guru pīru hāmā tā bhare jā murdāru na khāi.*

**SYNONYMS**  
*haku* — rights, rightful life and sustenance; *parāiā* — of another (violating another's life); *nānakā* — says Guru Nanak; *usu* — for him; *sūaru* — is like eating pork (taboo for Muslims); *usu* — for him; *gāi* — is like eating beef (sacrilege for Hindus); *guru pīru* — the true Guru or holy Prophet; *hāmā tā bhare* — will stand as an advocate and witness of salvation; *jā* — only when; *murdāru* — dead carcass, slaughtered carrion; *na khāi* — he does not devour.

**TRANSLATION**  
**"Guru Nanak declares: To usurp the rights and life of another is as abhorrent as consuming pork for a Muslim or devouring beef for a Hindu! A true Guru or spiritual prophet will stand as an intercessor for your liberation only when you do not consume dead carcasses [murdāru na khāi]!"**

**PURPORT**  
Guru Nanak Dev Ji categorically establishes that spiritual liberation is impossible for a person who feeds upon dead carcasses (*murdār*). Just as pork is an absolute spiritual taboo for Muslims and beef is an absolute sin for Hindus, taking the life of any creature for one's selfish consumption contaminates the soul with dark karmic pollution. Guru Nanak explicitly warns that neither a Guru nor a prophet will extend spiritual shelter to one who pollutes his mouth with the flesh of slaughtered creatures.  
In **Japji Sahib (Pauri 16)**, Guru Nanak defines the very foundation of cosmic religion:

> **ਧੌਲੁ ਧਰਮੁ ਦਇਆ ਕਾ ਪੂਤੁ ॥ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ ਥਾਪਿ ਰਖਿਆ ਜਿਨਿ ਸੂਤਿ ॥**  
> *"Dhaul dharamu dayā kā pūtu; santokhu thāpi rakhiā jini sūti."*  
> **"The mythical bull bearing the cosmic order is none other than Dharma, the direct offspring of boundless Compassion [Dayā], sustained by divine contentment."**  
> Where there is no compassion (*dayā*) for animals, true religion (*dharma*) ceases to exist.

---

#### 12.6.4 The Sacred Institution of Guru-kā-Langar: Pure Lacto-Vegetarianism:

When Guru Nanak founded the sacred community at Kartarpur, and when the Third Guru, **Guru Amar Das Ji**, formalized the egalitarian community kitchen known as **Guru-kā-Langar**, they established a permanent spiritual rule: **ਪਹਿਲੇ ਪੰਗਤਿ ਪਾਛੈ ਸੰਗਤਿ (*Pehle Pangat, Paache Sangat*)**—"First sit together in the egalitarian row to take sanctified food, and only then enter the congregation of the Guru."  
To ensure that all human beings—regardless of caste, religion, creed, or background—could eat together in absolute spiritual purity and harmony, **Guru-kā-Langar was established as strictly and exclusively lacto-vegetarian**:
1. **Total Exclusion of Meat, Fish, and Eggs:** For more than five centuries, across thousands of Gurdwaras worldwide (including the sacred *Harmandir Sahib* / Golden Temple at Amritsar), not a single gram of animal flesh, fish, or egg has ever been cooked, served, or permitted inside Guru-kā-Langar.
2. **Emperor Akbar’s Historical Visit:** When the Mughal Emperor Akbar visited Guru Amar Das Ji at Goindwal Sahib, the Emperor was required to sit on the floor alongside humble peasants and partake of the simple vegetarian langar (coarse rice, lentils, and bread) before he was granted an audience with the Guru. Akbar was so deeply moved by the sanctity, purity, and universal compassion of the langar that he offered vast tracts of land to the Guru's daughter.
3. **The Historical *Hukamnamas* (Divine Edicts):** The Tenth Master, **Guru Gobind Singh Ji**, issued historical edicts (*Hukamnamas*) prohibiting his Sikhs from consuming **ਕੁਠਾ (*Kuthā*)**—animal flesh slaughtered through ritual throat-slitting—and commanded his followers to cultivate *Dayā* (mercy) toward all beings. In the official Sikh code of conduct (*Rehat Maryada*), the slaughter and consumption of animals is recognized as a profound violation of spiritual sanctity.

---

fields.subTopic: Does Genesis 9:3 Command Christians and Jews to Eat Meat? The Post-Flood Concession Fallacy
fields.article:
#### 12.7.1 Objection 1: The Judeo-Christian Concession Fallacy (Genesis 9:3 vs. Genesis 1:29)

> **The Meat-Eater’s Theological Objection:**  
> *"In Genesis 9:3, God explicitly said to Noah after the Flood: 'Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.' Furthermore, Jesus ate the Passover lamb and multiplied fish for the multitudes. Therefore, meat-eating is divinely authorized by God in the Bible."*

##### The Scriptural Refutation:

1. **The Primordial Edenic Ideal Was 100% Vegan (Genesis 1:29):**  
   In the pristine paradise of the Garden of Eden—before human sin entered the world—God issued His first and eternal dietary law to mankind:
   > *"And God said: 'Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat [food].'"* (Genesis 1:29)  
   > In this original state of holiness, not a single animal was killed, slaughtered, or eaten. The Edenic diet was purely botanical.
2. **Genesis 9:3 Was a Temporary Emergency Concession (*Āpad-Dharma*), Not a Command:**  
   The concession in Genesis 9:3 was granted to Noah immediately following the cataclysmic global Deluge, when the entire Earth was submerged under water and all vegetation was completely destroyed. Just as ancient legal systems allow an individual stranded in a desert to eat anything to preserve life, God temporarily tolerated flesh-eating until crops could regrow.  
   Crucially, God did not bestow this concession as a blessing, but accompanied it with a terrifying curse of alienation and dread:
   > *"And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air... into your hand are they delivered."* (Genesis 9:2)  
   > Furthermore, God immediately attached a strict, absolute prohibition against consuming blood:  
   > *"But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat!"* (Genesis 9:4)
3. **The Prophetic Restored Kingdom Returns to Absolute Vegetarianism:**  
   When the prophets envision the coming of the Messianic Age and the redemption of the Earth, animal slaughter is completely eliminated:
   > *"The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them... and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord."* (Isaiah 11:6–9)  
   > If God's ultimate paradise is devoid of all killing, then participating in the slaughter of animals today is in direct opposition to God's divine will.
4. **Jesus's Radical Cleansing of the Temple: Stopping Animal Sacrifice:**  
   Modern readers overlook the true reason why Jesus cleansed the Temple of Jerusalem (Mark 11:15–18; John 2:14–16). The Temple courts had been converted into an enormous livestock market where cattle, sheep, and doves were bought and sold for bloody ritual slaughter. Jesus fashioned a whip, drove the animals out to set them free, overturned the moneychangers' tables, and quoted the Prophet Jeremiah:
   > *"Is it not written, 'My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer'? But ye have made it a den of thieves [Greek: spēlaion lēstōn — a cave of violent brigands]!"* (Mark 11:17)  
   > Jesus sacrificed His own life to overthrow the bloody sacrificial system of the Temple.
5. **The Historical Testimony of Early Church Fathers:**  
   Authentic early Christian records demonstrate that the immediate apostles and disciples of Christ abstained from all animal flesh:  
   \* **St. James the Just (Brother of Jesus):** The 2nd-century church historian Hegesippus (recorded by Eusebius in *Historia Ecclesiastica* II.23) records: *"James, the brother of the Lord, was holy from his mother's womb. He drank no wine nor strong drink, neither did he eat any animal flesh."*  
   \* **St. Matthew:** Clement of Alexandria records in *Paedagogus* (II.1): *"The Apostle Matthew lived upon seeds, nuts, hard berries, and vegetables, without flesh."*  
   \* **St. Peter:** In the early Christian texts *Clementine Homilies* (XII.6), Peter declares: *"I live on bread and olives alone, to which I rarely add any herbs."*  
   \* **St. Jerome (Translator of the Latin Vulgate):** *"Since Christ brought the end back to the beginning, we are no longer permitted to eat the dregs and stink of animal flesh."* (*Adversus Jovinianum* 1.30)

---

fields.subTopic: Is Meat-Eating and Animal Slaughter Mandated During Islamic Eid-ul-Adha (Qurbani)?
fields.article:
#### 12.7.2 Objection 2: The Islamic "Qurbani & Dhabihah" Mandate Fallacy

> **The Meat-Eater’s Theological Objection:**  
> *"Allah has permitted Halal meat in the Quran, and on Eid-al-Adha, animal sacrifice (Qurbani / Udhiyah) is an obligatory religious act. Rejecting meat is an un-Islamic innovation (bid'ah) and amounts to declaring forbidden (Haram) what Allah has made lawful (Halal)."*

##### The Scriptural Refutation:

1. **Eating Meat is Strictly *Mubah* (Permissible Concession), Never *Fard* (Obligatory):**  
   In Islamic jurisprudence (*Usul al-Fiqh*), actions are categorized into five moral divisions: *Fard* (obligatory), *Mustahabb* (recommended), *Mubah* (permissible / neutral), *Makruh* (disliked), and *Haram* (prohibited).  
   **No classical Islamic jurist has ever classified meat-eating as *Fard* (mandatory) or *Mustahabb* (recommended).** It is classified strictly as *Mubah*—a tolerated allowance granted to desert-dwelling nomadic tribes who had no access to fertile agricultural lands. Choosing a vegetarian diet out of compassion for God's creation is completely virtuous and in no way violates Islamic law.
2. **The True Spirit of Qurbani is Piety (*Taqwa*), Not Blood and Flesh:**  
   The Holy Quran explicitly clarifies the divine reality behind animal sacrifice, eradicating the pagan illusion that God desires animal blood:
   > **لَن يَنَالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَاؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ التَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ**  
   > *Lany-yanāla Allāha luḥūmuhā wa lā dimā'uhā wa lākiny-yanāluhu at-taqwā minkum.*  
   > **"Neither their meat nor their blood reaches Allah; what reaches Him is your personal piety and devotion [Taqwa]!"** (Surah Al-Hajj 22:37)  
   > The historical commemoration of Prophet Ibrahim's sacrifice represents the internal willingness to surrender one's ego and lust to God—not a ritualistic demand to slaughter billions of animals annually. In modern times, eminent Islamic scholars emphasize that fulfilling the spirit of Qurbani through financial charity (*Sadaqah*), grain distribution, or tree planting is far more faithful to the Quranic purpose than funding factory-farm slaughter.
3. **Prophet Muhammad's Dire Warning: Meat is Addictive like Wine:**  
   In the celebrated legal compendium **Muwatta Imam Malik** (Book 49, Hadith 3505), the second Caliph, **Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)**, issued an urgent spiritual warning to the Muslim community:
   > **إِيَّاكُمْ وَاللَّحْمَ فَإِنَّ لَهُ ضَرَاوَةً كَضَرَاوَةِ الْخَمْرِ**  
   > *Iyyākum wal-laḥma, fa-inna lahū ḍarāwatan ka-ḍarāwatil-khamr.*  
   > **"Beware of meat! For indeed, meat possesses an addictiveness just like the addictiveness of intoxicating wine!"**  
   > Caliph Umar was so alarmed by the spiritual dullness produced by flesh-eating that he strictly prohibited Muslims from buying or eating meat on two consecutive days, punishing those who indulged in regular flesh consumption.
4. **The Prophet’s Medical Verdict: Cow's Meat is Disease:**  
   The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) delivered an unequivocal medical diagnosis regarding bovine flesh, preserved in **Mustadrak al-Hakim** (Hadith 7438) and declared authentic (*Sahih*) by Imam al-Albani (*Sahih al-Jami* 4329):
   > **عَلَيْكُمْ بِأَلْبَانِ الْبَقَرِ فَإِنَّهَا شِفَاءٌ وَسَمْنِهَا فَإِنَّهُ دَوَاءٌ وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَلُحُومَهَا فَإِنَّ لُحُومَهَا دَاءٌ**  
   > *'Alaykum bi-albānil-baqari fa-innahā shifā'un, wa-samnihā fa-innahu dawā'un, wa-iyyākum wa-luḥūmahā fa-inna luḥūmahā dā'.*  
   > **"Make use of cow's milk, for it is a healing cure; make use of its clarified butter [ghee], for it is medicine; but beware of its meat, for its meat is disease [dā']!"**
5. **Modern Industrial Abattoirs Blatantly Violate Islamic *Dhabihah*:**  
   Islamic *Dhabihah* mandates that an animal must be raised humanely, given water before slaughter, never slaughtered in front of other animals, never have the knife sharpened in its sight, and be dispatched with absolute mercy. Today's commercial "Halal" abattoirs pack millions of terrorized cattle and chickens onto mechanized disassembly lines, shocking them, slicing their throats as they drown in blood, and treating them like mechanical commodities. Every bite of this factory-farmed meat violates the foundational Islamic principle of **إِحْسَان (*Ihsān* — universal excellence and tender compassion toward all creations)**.

---

fields.subTopic: Did Lord Buddha Permit Eating Meat Under the 'Threefold Purity' (Tikotiparisuddha) Rule?
fields.article:
#### 12.7.3 Objection 3: The Buddhist "Threefold Purity" (*Tikotiparisuddha*) Fallacy

> **The Meat-Eater’s Theological Objection:**  
> *"In the Theravada Vinaya, Lord Buddha allowed monks to eat meat under the 'threefold pure' rule (Tikotiparisuddha)—provided the monk did not see, hear, or suspect that the animal was slaughtered specifically for him. Therefore, buying meat at a butcher shop or supermarket is fully permissible for Buddhists."*

##### The Scriptural Refutation:

1. **The Vinaya Rule Was an Emergency Measure for Begging Mendicants Only:**  
   The "threefold purity" rule (*na diṭṭhaṁ, na sutaṁ, na parisaṅkitaṁ*) was strictly formulated for wandering, mendicant monks (*bhikkhus*) who owned no money, operated no kitchens, had no cooking utensils, and lived entirely on indiscriminate daily alms (*piṇḍapāta*). A mendicant monk was forbidden from asking for specific foods; whatever cold scrap a poor householder dropped into his alms bowl had to be eaten without attachment or pride.  
   **To stretch this begging concession into a license for modern householders to walk into a supermarket, spend cash, and purchase packaged cuts of dead animals is an outrageous intellectual distortion.**
2. **Economic Demand Directly Drives Slaughter (*Ghātaye*):**  
   In the *Dhammapada* (Verse 129), Lord Buddha commands:
   > **न हनेय्य न घातये (*Na haneyya na ghātaye*)** — *"One should neither kill nor cause another to kill!"*  
   > In modern capitalist economics, every purchase of meat at a restaurant or grocery store creates market demand. The abattoir slaughters animals precisely because consumers pay for carcasses. The buyer who hands over money is directly commanding the slaughter (*ghātaye*), and is fully implicated in the violent karma of the slaughterhouse.
3. **The Absolute Prohibition in the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*:**  
   Anticipating that future hypocrites would distort the begging rule to indulge their lust for meat, Lord Buddha issued an absolute, permanent, and universal prohibition in the **Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra (Chapter 8)**:
   > *"Mahāmati, there may be some foolish individuals in future times who will fabricate false discourses, claiming that I permitted meat-eating or partook of flesh Myself. But I declare unto you:* *Naiva mayā kasyacin-māṁsam anujñātaṁ, nānujānāmi, nānujñāsyāmi**—I have never permitted meat-eating to anyone, I do not permit it now, and I will never permit it under any circumstance!"*  
   > Lord Buddha explicitly states that animal slaughter exists exclusively because human beings eat meat:  
   > *"If no one consumes meat, then no slaughter of living beings will ever take place. Therefore, the consumer of meat and the slaughterer of the animal share identical guilt!"*
4. **The *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*: Meat Extinguishes Compassion:**  
   In the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* (Verse 32), Lord Buddha declares:
   > *"The eating of meat extinguishes the seed of Great Compassion [Mahā-Karuṇā]. Whosoever partakes of animal flesh terrifies all living creatures; animals flee from him in dread, sensing the scent of murder upon his breath."*

---

fields.subTopic: Do Vedic Injunctions Conceding Meat-Eating in Tantras Represent Spiritual Permission (Pravṛtti vs. Nivṛtti)?
fields.article:
#### 12.7.4 Objection 4: The Sanātana Dharma "Vedic Concession" Fallacy (*Pravṛtti* vs. *Nivṛtti*)

> **The Meat-Eater’s Theological Objection:**  
> *"The Vedic literature describes animal sacrifices (yajñas) in ancient times, and certain texts like Manusmṛti mention the offering of meat in ancestral rites (śrāddha). Therefore, Sanātana Dharma does not enforce universal vegetarianism, and meat-eating is a legitimate lifestyle choice."*

##### The Scriptural Refutation:

1. **The True Purpose of Vedic Concessions Was Ultimate Cessation (*Nivṛtti*):**  
   In the **Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (11.5.11)**, the great sage Nārada Muni explicitly clarifies the pedagogical strategy of the Vedas:
   > *loke vyavāyāmiṣa-madya-sevā nityāstu jantor na hi tatra codanā*  
   > *vyavasthitis teṣu vivāha-yajña-surā-grahair āsu nivṛttir iṣṭā*  
   > **"Conditioned living beings in this material world have a natural, disease-like addiction to meat-eating [āmiṣa], sex indulgence [vyavāya], and intoxication [madya]. The Vedic scriptures never encourage or order these activities [na hi tatra codanā]! Rather, the Vedas introduce restrictive regulations—such as marriage for sex, or rare complex sacrifices for meat—with the sole divine intent of gradually restricting and totally weaning them away toward absolute cessation [nivṛtti]!"**  
   > Just as a medical doctor administers small, diminishing doses of a substitute to safely detoxify a dangerous heroin addict, the Vedic regulations were designed to restrict barbarian meat-eaters until they gave up flesh entirely. To claim that the Vedas "recommend" meat-eating is as foolish as claiming a rehabilitation hospital recommends drug addiction!
2. **Manusmṛti’s Supreme Injunction: Cessation Yields the Ultimate Fruit:**  
   While *Manusmṛti* recognizes that meat-eating is a primitive instinct of conditioned souls (*pravṛtti*), it unambiguously commands *nivṛtti* as the supreme spiritual duty:
   > **न मांसभक्षणे दोषो न मद्ये न च मैथुने ।**  
   > **प्रवृत्तिरेषा भूतानां निवृत्तिस्तु महाफला ॥**  
   > *na māṁsa-bhakṣaṇe doṣo na madye na ca maithune*  
   > *pravṛttir eṣā bhūtānāṁ nivṛttis tu mahā-phalā* (Manusmṛti 5.56)  
   > **"There is no natural impediment in the material realm for indulging in meat, liquor, or sex, for this is the base animal instinct of all conditioned creatures [pravṛttir eṣā bhūtānāṁ]. But total cessation and detachment from these vices [nivṛttis tu] yields the supreme transcendental fruit of liberation [mahā-phalā]!"**
3. **Manusmṛti Declares All Eight Accomplices Guilty of Murder:**  
   *Manusmṛti* (5.51–52) leaves no legal loophole for the modern meat-consumer who claims, *"I did not kill the animal myself"*:
   > **अनुमन्ता विशसिता निहन्ता क्रयविक्रयी ।**  
   > **संस्कर्ता चोपहर्ता च खादकश्चेति घातकाः ॥**  
   > *anumantā viśasitā nihantā kraya-vikrayī*  
   > *saṁskartā copahartā ca khādakaś ceti ghātakāḥ*  
   > **"He who gives consent to the killing, he who carves the carcass, he who slays the creature, he who buys the meat, he who sells it, he who cooks it, he who serves it, and he who eats it—all eight of these individuals are equally murderers [ghātakāḥ] in the eyes of cosmic law!"**
4. **All Animal Sacrifices Are Strictly Prohibited in the Age of Kali:**  
   As established in Section 12.1 and Chapter 13, the *Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa* (185.180) and *Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta* (Madhya 6.259) categorically prohibit all animal sacrifices (*gavālambham* and *aśvamedham*) as well as flesh offerings in funeral rites (*pala-paitṛkam*) in Kali-yuga:
   > **कलौ पञ्च विवर्ജयेत् (*Kalau pañca vivarjayet*)** — *"In the Age of Kali, these five practices must be strictly and completely abandoned!"*  
   > Anyone who kills an animal today under the guise of Vedic ritual is an impious hypocrite destined for the darkest hells.

---

#### 12.7.5 Universal Comparative Theological Matrix:

The following matrix synthesizes the primordial divine ideal, the historical emergency concession, the true scriptural prohibition, and the ultimate spiritual goal across all world religions:

| Religious Tradition | Primordial Divine Ideal (State of Purity) | Historical Emergency Concession (Lower Stage) | Canonical Prohibition / Warning Against Meat | Ultimate Spiritual State / Restored Kingdom | Authoritative Canonical Citation |

| **Jainism** | Non-dual Empathy (*Parasparopagraho Jīvānām*) | Zero concession; complete abstinence required for all | 108 avenues of violent karma; dead flesh breeds micro-parasites | Total Liberation of the Soul (*Mokṣa*) | *Tattvārtha Sūtra 5.21; Ācārāṅga 1.2.3* |
